draft.title: Diamond and graphite
card: Diamond and graphite are both made only of carbon atoms. Each is a covalent network: atoms are joined by strong covalent bonds in a huge continuous lattice, not in small separate molecules.
each carbon atom bonds to four others in a three-dimensional lattice. All four valence electrons are held in bonds, so none are free to move. Diamond is very hard and does not conduct electricity.

each carbon atom bonds to three others in flat layers. The fourth electron is delocalised, meaning it can move along the layer. So graphite conducts electricity. The layers are held together by weak forces and slide over each other, so graphite is soft and slippery.
Uses follow from properties. Diamond suits cutting and drilling tools. Graphite suits pencil leads, lubricants and electrodes.
draft.remember: Diamond is hard because every carbon bonds in 3D. Graphite conducts because one electron per atom is free to move.

a.q: Why can graphite conduct electricity but diamond cannot?
opts: Graphite has delocalised electrons that move along its layers
Graphite has ions that can move when the solid is heated
Graphite has weaker covalent bonds within each layer
Graphite has more carbon atoms in its lattice than diamond
a.why: In graphite each carbon uses three electrons in bonds, and the fourth is delocalised and moves along the layer. In diamond all four electrons are held in bonds. The bonds within graphite layers are still strong, so weaker bonds are not the reason.
a.clue: Count how many electrons each carbon atom holds in bonds.

b.q: Priya's company needs a material for the tip of a drill that cuts through rock. Which material and reason suit best?
opts: Diamond, as each carbon bonds strongly to four others
Diamond, as it has delocalised electrons that hold it firm
Graphite, as its layers are strongly bonded to each other
Graphite, as each carbon bonds strongly to three others
b.why: A drill tip must be very hard. Diamond is hard because every carbon is bonded to four others in a rigid 3D lattice. Graphite also has strong bonds in each layer, but its layers slide because the forces between them are weak, so it is soft.
b.clue: Think about which structure cannot slide apart in layers.
